title: Five Winters and One Short Flag
subtitle: 体育赛事 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 体育赛事（人与社会·文学、艺术与体育）
meta: 主题语境：体育赛事（人与社会·文学、艺术与体育）　|　核心词汇：event　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 event 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1984 my brother ① held an event that no coach in the school would have entered, and he said the holding was the whole of the winter. The ② event, meaning the race itself and not the season, ran five winters and stayed unentered in the book; an event, he said, is the only thing in a school that is judged by how long it is left unentered.

Every ③ event in that school had the same short flag beside it, and the ④ event at the far side, meaning the one they kept for the final and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. An event, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to enter; my brother said the entering is the part that fills five winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the event was the whole of the year, meaning the occasion and not the race. The ⑥ event, meaning the occasion and not any of that, is the only thing in a year that everybody waits for and nobody enters; event, he said, is either something you hold or the only word that means both a race and an occasion. He said the occasion is the part they remember.

By 1989 the ⑦ event had become a line in a programme, and the programme had become an argument about the short flag. The ⑧ event of the whole thing, my brother wrote in January, was one school and five winters of entering; event, he said, is either the one at the far side or the reason you learned to enter. He said the entering was never mentioned.

The ⑨ event I remember is the one entered in the programme, which closed in 1991 and is still described as the quietest in the school. An ⑩ event, my mother said in 1993, is the only one that improves by being entered; every event, she said, is an occasion that has agreed to look like a race. She said the occasion was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 比赛项目；赛事（指学校里每一项旁边的那一项）
B. n. 赛事（指那一场比赛本身，与整个赛季相对）
C. 固定搭配：hold an event 举办一场赛事
D. n. 赛事（指留给决赛的那一场）
E. n. 赛事（抽象总称，指一所学校的赛事之事）
F. n. 赛事（指秩序册上写到、被排定的那一场）
G. n. 大事；活动（指一年里人人都等却无人报名的那样事情）
H. n. 活动（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人报名的那样事情）

items.q: held an event that no coach in the school would have entered
The event, meaning the race itself and not the season
the event at the far side

answers.why: hold an event 意为“举办一场赛事”，1984 年哥哥举办了一场学校里没有一位教练肯报名的赛事。
event 意为“赛事”，指那一场比赛本身而不是整个赛季，它经过了五个冬天而在簿子上没有记号。
event 意为“赛事”，指学校里每一项旁边的那一项，每一项旁边都有同一面短短的旗子。
event 意为“赛事”，指留给决赛的那一场，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
event 意为“大事、活动”，指一年里人人都等却无人报名的那样事情，叔叔说这件大事就是那一年的全部。
event 意为“活动”，指人人都等却无人报名的那样事情而不是那一场比赛，是一年里人人都等、却无人报名的东西。
event 意为“赛事”，指秩序册上写到、被排定的那一场，到 1989 年这一场成了秩序册里的一行。
event 意为“赛事”，哥哥一月写道，整件事的赛事之事是一所学校和五个冬天的报名。
event 意为“赛事”，我记得的是秩序册上排定的那一场，1991 年结束了，至今仍被说成学校里最安静的一场。
event 为抽象总称，母亲 1993 年说，一场赛事是唯一会因为被好好报名而变得更好的东西。
